newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihatsu launches new compact wagon.
newsitem.headline: Daihatsu launches new compact wagon.

text.p: Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd launched a new minivan-style compact wagon, the Pyzar, in Japan on Wednesday, Daihatsu president Iichi Shingu told a news conference.
The Pyzar comes with a 1.5-litre gasoline engine and dual airbags. The company has set a monthly sales target of 2,500 units and a base price of about 1.3 million yen.
The Pyzar is aimed at all age groups, Daihatsu said.

"We could lure people who want to buy multi-purpose vehicles, such as Honda's Odyssey and Toyota's Ipsum, as they are more expensive and bigger. The Pyzar is cheaper and easier to drive in the city because of its compact size," said Toyoaki Kohama, managing director in charge of domestic sales.
Prices for the Odyssey start at 1.79 million yen and at 1.92 million yen for the Ipsum.
Daihatsu, 33.4 percent owned by Toyota, will start exporting Pyzars to Southeast Asia and Europe later this year at a rate at 800 units a month.
